% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch19_cld_examples.tex and its included
% residual-Picard dossier.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$C$ be a smooth proper algebraic $K$-curve, and let
$W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$ be open.  Suppose that
$h\in C^0(W,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
\[
                         \dprimeddprime[h]=0.
\]
For a type~$2$ point $x\in W$, let $C_x$ be its smooth projective
residue curve and let
\[
 \operatorname{ob}_x(h)\in
 \operatorname{Pic}^0(C_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R
\]
be the residual class of the harmonic germ of $h$ at $x$.  Then the
following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h$ is ordinary CLD-smooth near $x$ and
      $\dprimeddprime h=0$ there as a smooth form;
\item $\operatorname{ob}_x(h)=0$.
\end{enumerate}
At points of types $1$, $3$, and $4$, the germ of $h$ is automatically
ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian.

Consequently, if
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p213-residual-picard-vanishing}
       \operatorname{Pic}^0(C_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R=0
       \qquad\text{for every type~$2$ point }x\in W,
\end{equation}
then $h$ is ordinary CLD-smooth on $W$ and
$\dprimeddprime h=0$ as a smooth form.  The hypothesis
\eqref{eq:p213-residual-picard-vanishing} holds, in particular, when the
residue field $\widetilde K$ is algebraic over a finite field, or when
$C$ is a Mumford curve.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch18_delta_forms.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-open-disc-descent}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, let $m\geq1$, and let $B$ be a good, topologically separated,
pure $m$-dimensional strict $K$-analytic space.  For
$R\in|K^\times|$, put
\[
 D_R^-=\{x\in(\mathbf A^1_K)^{\mathrm{an}}:|T(x)|<R\},
 \qquad X=B\times_KD_R^-,
\]
and write $\pi:X\to B$ and $q:X\to D_R^-$ for the projections.  If
$h\in C^0(X,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
\[
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0,
\]
then there is a unique $b\in C^0(B,\mathbf R)$ such that
\[
                         h=\pi^*b,
                         \qquad
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0.
\]
Moreover, $\mathrm d'[h]=0$ implies $\mathrm d'[b]=0$.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch18_delta_forms.tex.
\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p062-open-polyannulus-products-over-curves}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$C$ be a smooth proper algebraic curve, and let
$W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$ be open.  Let $s\geq0$, and for
$1\leq i\leq s$ put
\[
 A_i=A^-_{r_i,R_i}
 =\{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
                  r_i<|T_i(z)|<R_i\},
 \qquad 0<r_i<R_i,\quad r_i,R_i\in|K^\times|.
\]
Write
\[
 X_s=W\times_K\prod_{i=1}^sA_i,
 \qquad p:X_s\longrightarrow W,
 \qquad q_i:X_s\longrightarrow A_i.
\]
If $h\in C^0(X_s,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$, then there are unique continuous functions
$b,a_1,\ldots,a_s:W\to\mathbf R$ such that
\[
 h=p^*b+\sum_{i=1}^s(a_i\circ p)q_i^*\log|T_i|.
\]
Here $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0$, every $a_i$ is locally constant,
and $h$ is classically pluriharmonic.  In fact it is locally
$\mathbf R$-PL and Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.
\end{theorem}

% Source: manuscript/editorial/solver_dossiers_20260919/
% p062_mixed_exact_tower_transfer_20260919/STATEMENT.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, let $B_0$ be a positive-dimensional good, topologically separated,
pure strict $K$-analytic space, and let $\ell\geq1$.  Suppose that
\[
 B_\ell\xrightarrow{\pi_\ell}B_{\ell-1}
 \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow B_1
 \xrightarrow{\pi_1}B_0
\]
is a finite tower in which every $B_j$ is a positive-dimensional good,
topologically separated, pure strict $K$-analytic space.  At every stage
assume that exactly one of the following descriptions is specified.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial standard strict
open-polydisc bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-open-polydisc-bundle-descent}; in particular, its positive
fibre dimension and chart radii satisfy the conditions there.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial analytic projective-space
bundle as in \Cref{prop:p062-projective-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$(\mathbf P_K^{q_j})^{\mathrm{an}}$ for some $q_j\geq1$.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial smooth proper split-toric
bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-smooth-proper-split-toric-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$X_{\Sigma_j}^{\mathrm{an}}$ for a smooth proper split toric $K$-variety
$X_{\Sigma_j}$ of dimension $q_j\geq1$.
\item The field $K$ is algebraically closed, the base $B_{j-1}$ is locally
holomorphically separated and paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial
proper smooth curve bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-proper-smooth-curve-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$D_j^{\mathrm{an}}$ for a nonempty geometrically connected smooth proper
algebraic $K$-curve $D_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Put $\Pi=\pi_1\circ\cdots\circ\pi_\ell$.  If
$h\in C^0(B_\ell,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$, then there is a unique
$b\in C^0(B_0,\mathbf R)$ such that
\[
                  h=\Pi^*b,
                  \qquad \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0.
\]
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch15_poincare_lelong.tex.
\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:ch15-log-smooth}
Let $f$ be an invertible analytic function on an open set $U\subset X$.
Then $\log|f|$ is a smooth function on $U$ in the sense of ordinary CLD
forms, and
\[
 \dprime\log|f|=-\dprime t,\qquad
 \ddprime\log|f|=-\ddprime t,\qquad
 \dprimeddprime\log|f|=0,
\]
where $t$ is the affine coordinate on $\mathbf R$ pulled back by the moment
map $f$, that is, $t=-\log|f|$.
\end{lemma}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch13_forms.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:cld-form-pullback}
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of topologically separated analytic spaces.
There is a functorial morphism
\[
                 g^*:A_X^{p,q}\longrightarrow g_*A_Y^{p,q}
\]
commuting with wedge, $J$, $\dprime$, and $\ddprime$.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch16_bedford_taylor.tex.
\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:ch16-smooth-h}
Let $U$ be open in a good, topologically separated, pure, boundaryless
strict analytic space, let $T$ be a positive closed ordinary CLD current on
$U$, and let $u,v$ be continuous functions on $U$ satisfying
$\dprimeddprime[u]=\dprimeddprime[v]$.  If $h=u-v$ is ordinary CLD-smooth
and $\dprimeddprime h=0$, then
$\dprimeddprime(hT)=0$, equivalently
$\dprimeddprime(uT)=\dprimeddprime(vT)$.
\end{corollary}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part6/ch72_major_open_problems.tex.
\begin{problem}
\label{prob:frontier-cross-fan-upstairs}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field, let $n\geq2$, and let $X$
be a good separated strict boundaryless pure $n$-dimensional
$K$-analytic space.  Determine whether every positive
$\mathrm d'$- and $\mathrm d''$-closed CLD current $T$ of bidegree
$(p,p)$, $0\leq p\leq n-1$, has the following property: for every open
$W\subseteq X$ and all continuous psh functions $U,V$ on $W$,
\[
                  \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[U]
                  =\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[V]
\]
implies
\[
 \mathrm d'\mathrm d''\bigl(U\,T|_W\bigr)
 =\mathrm d'\mathrm d''\bigl(V\,T|_W\bigr).
\]
If this fails, construct a counterexample.
\end{problem}

% Book-local P21.3 residual-Picard open-polycylinder tower package,
% 20 September 2026.
\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower}
Let $K,C,W$ be as in
\Cref{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve}, and assume
\eqref{eq:p213-residual-picard-vanishing}.  Fix integers $s\geq1$ and
$r\geq0$.  Let $\pi_0:Y_0\to W$ be a morphism, where $Y_0$ is a good,
topologically separated, pure $(s+r+1)$-dimensional strict $K$-analytic
space.  Suppose that $W$ has an analytic open cover by sets $U$ for which,
with radii
\[
 \begin{gathered}
  0<r_{U,i}<R_{U,i},\qquad
  r_{U,i},R_{U,i}\in|K^\times|\quad(1\leq i\leq s),\\
  \rho_{U,j}\in|K^\times|\quad(1\leq j\leq r),
 \end{gathered}
\]
there is an isomorphism over $U$
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-chart}
 \pi_0^{-1}(U)\simeq
 U\times_K\prod_{i=1}^s
 \{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
              r_{U,i}<|T_{U,i}(z)|<R_{U,i}\}
 \times_K\prod_{j=1}^rD^-_{\rho_{U,j}}.
\end{equation}

Put $B_0=Y_0$.  Let $\ell\geq0$, and, when $\ell\geq1$, suppose that
\[
 B_\ell\xrightarrow{\pi_\ell}B_{\ell-1}
 \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow B_1
 \xrightarrow{\pi_1}B_0
\]
is a finite tower satisfying the stagewise hypotheses of
\Cref{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer}.  Write
$\Pi=\pi_1\circ\cdots\circ\pi_\ell$ when $\ell\geq1$ and
$\Pi=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}$ when $\ell=0$.

If $h\in C^0(B_\ell,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
$\dprimeddprime[h]=0$, then there is a unique
$g\in C^0(Y_0,\mathbf R)$ such that
\[
                    h=\Pi^*g,
                    \qquad \dprimeddprime[g]=0.
\]
Both $g$ and $h$ are ordinary CLD-smooth and have zero smooth Hessian.
No compatibility of the annular coordinates in
\eqref{eq:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-chart} is required on
overlaps; in particular, no vanishing of the integral monodromy or of the
zero-current radiance class is assumed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-bt}
In the setting of
\Cref{thm:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower}, assume that
$B=B_\ell$ is boundaryless of pure dimension $n\geq2$.  Let $T$ be a
positive $\mathrm d'$- and $\mathrm d''$-closed ordinary CLD current of
bidegree $(p,p)$, $0\leq p\leq n-1$, and let
$u,v\in C^0(B,\mathbf R)$ satisfy
\[
                         \dprimeddprime[u]=\dprimeddprime[v].
\]
Then
\[
                         \dprimeddprime(uT)=\dprimeddprime(vT).
\]
In particular, this holds for every continuous psh pair in the
continuous-potential predicate of P21.3.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-cover-bt}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$X$ be a good, topologically separated, pure, boundaryless strict
$K$-analytic space of dimension $n\geq2$, and let $V\subseteq X$ be
ordinary open.  Suppose that $V$ has an ordinary open cover by sets $B$
which, with their induced analytic structures, satisfy the geometric
hypotheses of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-bt}.  Then
every positive closed ordinary CLD current $T$ of bidegree $(p,p)$ on $V$,
$0\leq p\leq n-1$, has Bedford--Taylor independence for every continuous
psh pair $u,v$ on $V$ with equal Hessian currents.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-basis-bt}
Let $K$ and $X$ be as in
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-cover-bt}.
Suppose that the ordinary topology of $X$ has a basis of open sets $B$ such
that every $B$, with its induced analytic structure, satisfies the
geometric hypotheses of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-bt}.  Then the
continuous-pair Bedford--Taylor predicate in P21.3 holds on every ordinary
open subset of $X$ for every positive closed ordinary CLD current.
\end{corollary}
proof:
\begin{proof}[Proof of
\Cref{thm:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower}]
If $\ell\geq1$, apply
\Cref{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer} to descend $h$ uniquely
to a continuous function $g$ on $Y_0$ with
\[
                         h=\Pi^*g,
                         \qquad \dprimeddprime[g]=0.
\]
For $\ell=0$, take $g=h$; uniqueness is then tautological.

It remains to prove ordinary smoothness locally on $Y_0$.  Fix a chart
\eqref{eq:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-chart}, and let
\[
 Z_U=U\times_K\prod_{i=1}^s
 \{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
              r_{U,i}<|T_{U,i}(z)|<R_{U,i}\}.
\]
The open set $U$ and every standard strict annular or disc factor are good,
topologically separated, pure, and strict.  Their finite products, including
each intermediate base obtained while removing the disc factors, retain
these properties and have positive dimension.
Successive applications of \Cref{prop:p062-open-disc-descent} to the $r$
open-disc factors give a continuous function $\bar g_U$ on $Z_U$ such that
\[
 g|_{\pi_0^{-1}(U)}=\operatorname{pr}_{Z_U}^*\bar g_U,
 \qquad \dprimeddprime[\bar g_U]=0;
\]
when $r=0$, this means simply $\bar g_U=g|_{\pi_0^{-1}(U)}$ under the
displayed chart.

Apply \Cref{thm:p062-open-polyannulus-products-over-curves} to $\bar g_U$.
Writing $p_U:Z_U\to U$ and $q_{U,i}:Z_U\to A_{U,i}$ for the projections,
there are a continuous zero-current function $b_U$ on $U$ and locally
constant functions $a_{U,1},\ldots,a_{U,s}$ on $U$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p213-residual-picard-local-polycylinder-formula}
 \bar g_U=p_U^*b_U+
 \sum_{i=1}^s(a_{U,i}\circ p_U)q_{U,i}^*\log|T_{U,i}|.
\end{equation}
The residual-Picard criterion
\Cref{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve} applies on $U$ and makes
$b_U$ ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian.  After shrinking in
$U$, all $a_{U,i}$ are constant.  Each $T_{U,i}$ is an invertible analytic
function on its annulus, so \Cref{lem:ch15-log-smooth} makes
$\log|T_{U,i}|$ ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian.  Therefore
\eqref{eq:p213-residual-picard-local-polycylinder-formula} makes
$\bar g_U$ ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian.  Pullback along
$\operatorname{pr}_{Z_U}$ has the same properties by
\Cref{prop:cld-form-pullback}.  The displayed charts cover $Y_0$, so $g$
is ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian on $Y_0$.

Finally, functorial pullback of ordinary CLD forms commutes with both
differentials by \Cref{prop:cld-form-pullback}.  Hence
$h=\Pi^*g$ is ordinary CLD-smooth and has zero smooth Hessian.  The proof
was chartwise and imposed no overlap condition on the annular coordinates,
which proves the final scope assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-bt}]
Put $h=u-v$.  The equality of Hessian currents gives
$\dprimeddprime[h]=0$.  The tower theorem makes $h$ ordinary CLD-smooth
with zero smooth Hessian.  Apply \Cref{cor:ch16-smooth-h}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-cover-bt}]
Put $h=u-v$.  On every member $B$ of the displayed cover, apply
\Cref{thm:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower} to $h|_B$.
Thus $h$ is ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian locally on $V$.
These are sheaf-local properties, so they hold on $V$.  Apply
\Cref{cor:ch16-smooth-h} directly to $T,u,v$ on $V$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-basis-bt}]
For an ordinary open $V\subseteq X$, the basis members contained in $V$
form a cover to which
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-open-polycylinder-mixed-tower-cover-bt}
applies.
\end{proof}
